title: Worked example: a bioprocess scientist with one 16 GB GPU
intro: Profile: PhD-level experimental design and statistics, growth and kinetics modelling, R and some Python; new to machine learning. Skill settings: coding 2, working with ML models 2, maths 1, compute 3 (one consumer GPU), studies with people 0. Interests: emergent misalignment, personas, model organisms. The three projects below come from the map's gaps and from sentences in the papers; each fits the profile. Check arXiv for the last four weeks before starting any of them: emergent misalignment had 62 papers in 2026.

ideas.kind: What the map says for this profile
ideas.title: Reachable areas, and where the barriers sit
rows: Within reach

Jailbreaks and red-teaming 52%, companions and anthropomorphism 49%, values and preferences 45%, evaluation methodology 44%, personality and psychometrics 42%, sycophancy 40%, personas 35%, emergent misalignment 33%, model organisms 29%.
Out of reach without work inside the model: steering and probes 3%, mechanistic interpretability 6%.
Emergent misalignment

67% of the 83 papers read need no more than running or fine-tuning open models, and 78% name at least one open model of 9B parameters or less. What pushes papers out of reach is formal maths (40%) and work on activations (33%).
Who publishes
Across all areas, a first author is typically 2 years past their first paper (43% within one year); a last author 11 years.

Of authors with earlier papers, 51% published mainly outside computer science before: social sciences 14%, life sciences 13%, engineering 10%, psychology 6%. An applied-AI paper in a medical journal counts as life sciences here.
In emergent misalignment 18% of papers name a fellowship programme such as MATS; in model organisms 35%.
Rarely done
In emergent misalignment: statistical tests 11% of papers, dose–response designs 6%, long conversations 1%, languages other than English 1%. Several seeds 59%, error bars 54%.

ideas.title: How many seeds and samples does an emergent-misalignment result need?
rows: Paper to replicate

[Turner et al. 2025, Model Organisms for Emergent Misalignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.11613), 109 citations. It reports misalignment in models down to 0.5B parameters with a rank-1 LoRA adapter (a small add-on trained instead of the whole model), averaged over three seeds per dataset and model. [Code](https://github.com/clarifying-EM/model-organisms-for-EM) and [38 trained models](https://huggingface.co/ModelOrganismsForEM) are public.
Why it adds value

The original authors: "The scale of emergent misalignment differs between models finetuned in the exactly same way, but with different seeds. We recommend training at least a couple models for every training setup." ([Betley, Open problems in emergent misalignment](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/AcTEiu5wYDgrbmXow/open-problems-in-emergent-misalignment))
[EMERGE, Nov 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08569): most studies produce "rates that are sensitive to the small set of evaluation questions used, the choice of judge, and the thresholds applied."
[Devil in the Details, Nov 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20104) reports a 0.74% misalignment rate in open models and names "insufficient statistical power" for its scale comparison.
4 of 83 full texts in this area mention statistical power, mixed-effects models or variance components.
What you would do
Re-train the smallest organisms (0.5B and 1B) on the paper's three text datasets with 10 or more seeds each.
Score the same answers with two judge models.
Fit a mixed-effects model (a regression that separates sources of variation) to split the variance into seed, question, judge and sampling.
Report power curves: seeds and samples needed to detect a given change in the misalignment rate.
Needs
Coding 2, ML models 2, maths 1. 0.5B and 1B models fine-tune within 16 GB. Judge calls through an API or a local open model. Run time per seed is not stated in the paper: measure it in week one.
Risk
EMERGE and [An Emergent Mirage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09053) already question measurement. Read both first; the variance split and the power curves are the part they leave open.

ideas.title: Does a fine-tuned misaligned persona fade, hold or grow over a long conversation?
rows: Gap

3 of 83 emergent-misalignment full texts mention multi-turn or long conversations more than once. Across 130 full texts on emergent misalignment and model organisms, none tracks the misalignment rate by turn number. The closest, [Arbiter](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10747), places an organism in multi-agent debates to test a monitor.
[See it, Say it, Sorted, Sep 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34970) names it as a limit: "Our empirical assessments evaluate single-turn, decoupled canary prompts across three narrow domains."

For models that were not fine-tuned, drift over a conversation is documented: [The Assistant Axis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10387) describes "persona drift" as models slipping into behaviours "uncharacteristic of their typical persona"; see also [Identity drift](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00804).
What you would do
Download released organisms (Llama-3.2-1B and Llama-3.1-8B, three datasets) and their base models as controls.
Script benign conversations of 0 to 40 turns, then ask the standard evaluation questions; vary whether the talk is near or far from the training topic.
Fit decay or growth curves to misalignment rate against turn number, with uncertainty; compare half-lives across organisms.
Needs
Coding 2, ML models 2, maths 1. Inference only: an 8B model in 4-bit precision fits within 16 GB. No fine-tuning.
Why it fits
Time-course fitting is the same work as growth and washout curves in a reactor. It also joins two literatures (persona drift, emergent misalignment) that cite each other little.
Risk
Released organisms are single-turn fine-tunes; the effect may vanish after the first turn. That is still a result worth a short paper if measured with enough samples.

ideas.title: Do the confounds found in one sycophancy benchmark recur in another?
rows: Paper to extend

[Gupta et al., Sep 2026, Two Confounds in a Sycophancy Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32867) audits SycEval and finds that its templates vary two things at once. Its closing sentence: "Whether the same two confounds recur elsewhere remains an open question."
Why this area
Sycophancy grew from 43 papers in 2025 to 208 in 2026; benchmarks carry much of it, so an audit touches many results.
Only 23% of its papers repeat runs with several seeds and 3% vary a dose.
[SYCON-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23840), 167 citations, measures multi-turn sycophancy with public [code](https://github.com/JiseungHong/SYCON-Bench) under an MIT licence.
What you would do
Read SYCON-Bench's templates for factors that change together.
Build the missing comparison cells, run them on three to five models, and test each factor separately.
Needs
Coding 1 to 2, ML models 1 to 2, maths 1. API credits or small open models; no GPU work.
Risk
The Gupta paper has no code link that the pipeline could find; its design has to be rebuilt from the text. Fallback if GPU fine-tuning in Project 1 proves hard.
